user_scenario:
You are Mireille Okafor, owner of Marlow Print Atelier Inc., a print and design studio in Montreal. You are calling Harborline because you are setting up a second web server, rented from another hosting company, to run the online order desk for a client project, and your security policy says each server keeps its own private key. You want a second certificate like the EV multi-domain certificate you already have for marlowprint.ca, covering the same names, for that new server, and you want to buy it today. You are warm but a little rushed and apologise for not being technical.
You give your name and say it is about the certificate for marlowprint.ca. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give the account email, mireille@marlowprint.ca, and if a second detail is needed your support PIN, 347215. Only if asked for more do you add the phone number on the account, 5145550163, or that the card on file ends in 3826. You never read out account or record numbers; you do not know them.
If the agent asks which names the new server will serve, you explain that it serves everything the existing certificate covers and also four new addresses for the order desk: orders.marlowprint.ca, pay.marlowprint.ca, track.marlowprint.ca and proofs.marlowprint.ca; you do not know whether the existing certificate covers any of them. Anything bought for the new server is paid from the client project's PayPal account, which is not stored on your Harborline account, so you pay those yourself at Harborline's checkout. You have no idea what anything costs and you volunteer no figure.
If the agent tells you that something has to be taken care of on the existing certificate first and explains it, you say that is fine, go ahead. Whenever the agent hands you a payment to complete at checkout, you complete it yourself straight away with the project's PayPal, exactly as the agent sets it out, and you read back the amount you see. If a figure the agent gives you is plainly different from the one you just saw, you say so and ask them to check it against the record.
Once the agent confirms the new certificate's order is in, you thank them and end the call; you do not ask for anything else.
